item: C1: opposite-endpoint return map g on extremal directions, whose Kuratowski contraction factor (1-M/r)(1-M/s) <= (1-M/(1+t))^2 < 1 is supplied by the hypothetical attained defect M, so that Darbo's theorem gives aligned chords (paper I10+I15 -> I16, prop:alignment; provisional N3, F3+F5)
item_type: F3+F5 (auxiliary construction + re-representation of the extremal problem as a chi-contraction fixed-point problem); a lemma-level device, not a witness
lean_status_why: ReturnMap.lean defines exactly the paper's g (eq:return) and its radii p,s,u,r, ReturnMapEstimate/ReturnMapBounds/ReturnMapNoncompactness prove eq:contraction, the factor (1-M/(1+t))^2 and chi(gH) <= gamma chi(H) for every H in C, and Alignment.lean feeds them to a re-proved Darbo theorem to get prop:alignment; exists_alignedConfiguration is on the comparator's only path to M = 0 (no_attained_positive_defect).
lean_gaps: Route identical to the paper (radial contacts, extremal set E, r = u + M, two triangle inequalities, scalar binning of p and u, Darbo). No weaker or special-case statement: the comparator OAI.Tingley.tingley_sphere_isometry_full matches the headline exactly (uniqueness even among non-continuous linear maps).

Totalization: for the Darbo step g is extended to all of X as returnAmbient (value 0 off the unit sphere, likewise pAmbient/sAmbient/uAmbient/rAmbient); only ContinuousOn the sphere is proved. The paper works on S_X directly. Harmless: C is inside E ⊂ S_X.

Lean splits the device into a map-agnostic abstraction: exists_fixedPoint_of_return_estimate (any continuous g : X → X on a nonempty closed bounded convex C in a Banach space, any scalar functions p,s,u,r with radii in [1-t,1+t], s = p + M, r = u + M and the paper's two-point estimate, has a fixed point). The paper states this inline only for its g. For downstream reuse this is the cleaner library interface.

Darbo is re-proved (CondensingFixedPoint.lean via nested condensing sets with chi -> 0, compact convex intersection, then Schauder via Sperner/Brouwer on simplices); Mathlib d13f23b has none of chi, Darbo, Schauder or Brouwer. This is N0 background (39% of the target DAG) and not part of C1.

The device is applied to the completed-ultrapower isometry produced by positive_maxDefect_attained_or_inverse (DefectAttainment.lean), not to the original f; the paper does the same (lem:attainment). exists_alignedConfiguration assumes CompleteSpace X, HasDefectBound f M for all q in [0,1] and attainment signedDefect f t x0 y = M.
The invariant convex set C comes from C2 (exists_return_invariant_convex, positive hull-growth schedule); C1 needs it as input. C1 alone does not give alignment.
Minor bookkeeping: the paper's r||g(v)-g(v')|| <= |r-r'| + |u-u'| + u||w-w'|| becomes 2|u-u'| + u||w-w'|| in Lean, using r-r' = u-u' on E; same estimate.

lean_source.name: OAI.Tingley.{pRadius,xPoint,sRadius,wDirection,uRadius,zPoint,rRadius,returnSphere}
lean_source.kind: def (the return map g and its four radii)
lean_source.text:
/-- The first radial radius. The isometry is an explicit common parameter even
though this first contact only uses the domain center. -/
def pRadius (_f : UnitSphere X ≃ᵢ UnitSphere Y) (y : UnitSphere X)
    (t : ℝ) (ht : 0 < t ∧ t < 1) (v : UnitSphere X) : ℝ :=
  radialRadius (t • (y : X)) (returnCenter_lt_one y t ht) v

variable (f : UnitSphere X ≃ᵢ UnitSphere Y) (y : UnitSphere X)
variable (t : ℝ) (ht : 0 < t ∧ t < 1)

/-- The first contact point `t y + p v`. -/
def xPoint (v : UnitSphere X) : UnitSphere X :=
  ⟨t • (y : X) + pRadius f y t ht v • (v : X),
    norm_radialRadius (t • (y : X)) (returnCenter_lt_one y t ht) v⟩

def sRadius (v : UnitSphere X) : ℝ :=
  ‖(f (xPoint f y t ht v) : Y) - t • (f y : Y)‖

/-- The image-side outward unit direction. -/
def wDirection (v : UnitSphere X) : UnitSphere Y :=
  normalize ((f (xPoint f y t ht v) : Y) - t • (f y : Y))
    (unit_sub_center_ne_zero (f (xPoint f y t ht v)) (f y) t ht)

/-- The second radial contact uses the negative of the actual direction `w`. -/
def uRadius (v : UnitSphere X) : ℝ :=
  radialRadius (t • (f y : Y)) (returnCenter_lt_one (f y) t ht)
    (sphereNeg (wDirection f y t ht v))

def zPoint (v : UnitSphere X) : UnitSphere X :=
  f.symm (radialContact (t • (f y : Y)) (returnCenter_lt_one (f y) t ht)
    (sphereNeg (wDirection f y t ht v)))

def rRadius (v : UnitSphere X) : ℝ :=
  ‖(zPoint f y t ht v : X) - t • (y : X)‖

/-- The genuine return map on the unit sphere. -/
def returnSphere (v : UnitSphere X) : UnitSphere X :=
  normalize (t • (y : X) - (zPoint f y t ht v : X))
    (center_sub_unit_ne_zero (zPoint f y t ht v) y t ht)

lean_source.name: OAI.Tingley.returnSphere_pair_estimate
lean_source.text:
/-- The exact two-point estimate for the constructed return map on its actual
extremal sphere set. Both endpoint comparisons use the original sphere isometry. -/
theorem returnSphere_pair_estimate
    (f : UnitSphere X ≃ᵢ UnitSphere Y) (y : UnitSphere X)
    (t : ℝ) (ht : 0 < t ∧ t < 1) (M : ℝ) (hb : HasDefectBound f M)
    {v v' : UnitSphere X}
    (hv : v ∈ extremalSphere f y t ht M)
    (hv' : v' ∈ extremalSphere f y t ht M) :
    ‖(returnSphere f y t ht v : X) - (returnSphere f y t ht v' : X)‖ ≤
      (uRadius f y t ht v * pRadius f y t ht v /
        (rRadius f y t ht v * sRadius f y t ht v)) * ‖(v : X) - (v' : X)‖ +
      2 * |uRadius f y t ht v - uRadius f y t ht v'| / rRadius f y t ht v +
      2 * uRadius f y t ht v * |pRadius f y t ht v - pRadius f y t ht v'| /
        (rRadius f y t ht v * sRadius f y t ht v) := by

lean_source.name: OAI.Tingley.chi_return_image_le
lean_source.text:
/-- The exact all-subsets contraction, including the empty subset. The scalar
relations and the two-point estimate are supplied by the actual return map. -/
theorem chi_return_image_le
    {X : Type*} [PseudoMetricSpace X]
    {C : Set X} {g : X → X} {p s u r : X → ℝ} {t M : ℝ}
    (ht0 : 0 < t) (ht1 : t < 1) (hM : 0 < M)
    (hCne : C.Nonempty) (hCb : Bornology.IsBounded C)
    (_hgC : Set.MapsTo g C C)
    (hbounds : ∀ v ∈ C,
      (1 - t ≤ p v ∧ p v ≤ 1 + t) ∧
      (1 - t ≤ s v ∧ s v ≤ 1 + t) ∧
      (1 - t ≤ u v ∧ u v ≤ 1 + t) ∧
      (1 - t ≤ r v ∧ r v ≤ 1 + t))
    (hs : ∀ v ∈ C, s v = p v + M)
    (hr : ∀ v ∈ C, r v = u v + M)
    (hpair : ∀ v ∈ C, ∀ v' ∈ C,
      dist (g v) (g v') ≤
        (u v * p v / (r v * s v)) * dist v v' +
        2 * |u v - u v'| / r v +
        2 * u v * |p v - p v'| / (r v * s v))
    {H : Set X} (hHC : H ⊆ C) :
    chi (g '' H) ≤ (1 - M / (1 + t)) ^ 2 * chi H := by

lean_source.name: OAI.Tingley.exists_fixedPoint_of_return_estimate
lean_source.text:
/-- The radius bounds and two-point estimate imply an actual fixed point.
The hypotheses contain neither a noncompactness estimate nor a fixed-point
principle: both are supplied by the preceding constructive proofs. -/
theorem exists_fixedPoint_of_return_estimate
    {C : Set X} {g : X → X} {p s u r : X → ℝ} {t M : ℝ}
    (ht0 : 0 < t) (ht1 : t < 1) (hM : 0 < M)
    (hCne : C.Nonempty) (hCclosed : IsClosed C)
    (hCb : Bornology.IsBounded C) (hCconvex : Convex ℝ C)
    (hg : ContinuousOn g C) (hgC : Set.MapsTo g C C)
    (hbounds : ∀ v ∈ C,
      (1 - t ≤ p v ∧ p v ≤ 1 + t) ∧
      (1 - t ≤ s v ∧ s v ≤ 1 + t) ∧
      (1 - t ≤ u v ∧ u v ≤ 1 + t) ∧
      (1 - t ≤ r v ∧ r v ≤ 1 + t))
    (hs : ∀ v ∈ C, s v = p v + M)
    (hr : ∀ v ∈ C, r v = u v + M)
    (hpair : ∀ v ∈ C, ∀ v' ∈ C,
      dist (g v) (g v') ≤
        (u v * p v / (r v * s v)) * dist v v' +
        2 * |u v - u v'| / r v +
        2 * u v * |p v - p v'| / (r v * s v)) :
    ∃ x ∈ C, g x = x := by

structure AlignedConfiguration
    (f : UnitSphere X ≃ᵢ UnitSphere Y) (y : UnitSphere X) (t M : ℝ) where
  x : UnitSphere X
  z : UnitSphere X
  v : UnitSphere X

  s : ℝ
  u : ℝ

  r_pos : 0 < r
  s_pos : 0 < s
  u_pos : 0 < u
  x_eq : (x : X) = t • (y : X) + p • (v : X)
  z_eq : (z : X) = t • (y : X) - r • (v : X)
  fx_eq : (f x : Y) = t • (f y : Y) + s • (w : Y)
  fz_eq : (f z : Y) = t • (f y : Y) - u • (w : Y)
  s_sub_p : s - p = M
  r_sub_u : r - u = M
  chord_sum : p + r = s + u
  chord_le_two : p + r ≤ 2

lean_source.name: OAI.Tingley.exists_fixedPoint_of_kuratowski_contraction
lean_source.text:
/-- A continuous self-map satisfying the actual all-subsets Kuratowski
contraction has a fixed point. No compactness premise on `C` is required. -/
theorem exists_fixedPoint_of_kuratowski_contraction
    {C : Set E} (hne : C.Nonempty) (hclosed : IsClosed C)
    (hbounded : Bornology.IsBounded C) (hconv : Convex ℝ C)
    {g : E → E} (hg : ContinuousOn g C) (hmap : MapsTo g C C)
    {γ : ℝ} (hγ0 : 0 ≤ γ) (hγ1 : γ < 1)
    (hχ : ∀ H : Set E, H ⊆ C → chi (g '' H) ≤ γ * chi H) :
    ∃ x ∈ C, g x = x := by

speedup_targets.title: S1. Finite-dimensional stability of sphere isometries (Vestfrid): ε-isometries of the unit spheres of ℓ2^n, ℓ∞^n and ℓ1^n are uniformly close to linear isometries
speedup_targets.statement: If f : S_X → S_X (X = ℓ2^n, ℓ∞^n or ℓ1^n) is a surjective ε-isometry, |‖f(x)-f(y)‖-‖x-y‖| ≤ ε, then there is a linear isometry T with sup_{x∈S_X} ‖f(x)-Tx‖ ≤ C(n)·ε (exact constants not verified).
speedup_targets.reference: I. A. Vestfrid, 'Near-isometries of the unit sphere', Ukrainian Math. J. 72(4) (2020) (ℓ2^n, ℓ∞^n); I. A. Vestfrid, 'ε-isometries of the unit sphere in ℓ1^n', Colloq. Math. 177 (2024) 127-133, DOI 10.4064/cm9491-1-2025. Abstracts only (search summaries); full texts not read.
speedup_targets.current_proof_size: ~7 pp (ℓ1^n paper, pp. 127-133); UMJ paper length not verified. No Lean formalization anywhere found.
speedup_targets.how_item_helps: The device turns an attained extremal defect into an exact fixed-point configuration. With ε-slack, extremality gives r ≥ u + M - ε and s = p + M on E, so the two-point estimate becomes γ·dist + scalar oscillation + O(ε) with γ = (1-M/(1+t))^2. A χ-contraction with additive error gives an invariant convex set of χ ≤ O(ε)/(1-γ) = O(ε/M), i.e. approximately aligned chords; a quantitative chord contradiction would then bound M ≤ C√ε (or Cε^α) uniformly in n. This would replace three class-specific arguments by one dimension-free argument. The final step (approximately radial T ⇒ near a linear isometry) is NOT supplied by the device and is a real gap (Omladič-Šemrl/Hyers-Ulam need a uniform global ε-isometry; T is only ε·‖x‖-close).
speedup_targets.expected_speedup: low-med (paper level: a uniform proof is plausible but the rate may be worse than Vestfrid's; Lean: the existing lemmas are stated for exact isometries f : UnitSphere X ≃ᵢ UnitSphere Y and must be re-proved with slack)
speedup_targets.counts_as: device reuse (the theorem of 322 does not imply ε-stability)

open_problems.title: O1. Dimension-free stability of Tingley's problem (ε-isometries of unit spheres)
open_problems.statement: Is there a universal C (and α > 0) such that for all real Banach spaces X, Y and every surjective ε-isometry f : S_X → S_Y there is a surjective linear isometry T : X → Y with sup_{x∈S_X} ‖f(x) - Tx‖ ≤ C ε^α?
open_problems.reference: Vestfrid UMJ 2020 and Colloq. Math. 2024/25 (finite-dim classes only); Hyers-Ulam / Omladič-Šemrl 1995 (whole spaces, 2ε sharp); Matoušková, 'Almost isometries of balls', JFA 190 (2002) 507-525 (bi-Lipschitz near-isometries of Euclidean balls far from isometries: a warning that the multiplicative version fails). URLs: https://umj.imath.kiev.ua/index.php/umj/article/view/6049 ; https://impan.pl/en/publishing-house/journals-and-series/colloquium-mathematicum/all/177/1/115838/varepsilon-isometries-of-the-unit-sphere-in-ell-n-1
open_problems.status: open as far as found (no general result in searches; not verified against a problem list)
open_problems.obstruction_match: Exactly C1's obstruction with a quantitative twist: no compactness, so an approximately extremal configuration must be aligned by a dimension-free fixed-point argument; the defect M is again the only source of a contraction margin.
open_problems.adaptation_sketch: (1) define D_q as in 322; attainment in ultrapowers survives (ε-isometries pass to ultrapowers with the same ε). (2) On E_ε = {s - p ≥ M - ε}, triangle equalities hold up to O(ε): r ≥ u + M - O(ε). (3) The two-point estimate gives χ(gH) ≤ γχ(H) + O(ε) with γ = (1-M/(1+t))^2; the Darbo iteration gives a nonempty compact-modulo-O(ε/M) invariant convex set and approximate fixed points (Lean: needs an additive-error variant of chi_return_image_le). (4) Quantitative versions of the secant lemma and chord contradiction give M ≤ C ε^α. (5) Gap: from 'radial extension has defect ≤ Cε^α' to 'near a linear isometry' needs an approximate Mazur-Ulam for positively homogeneous maps, which is not standard.
open_problems.payoff: high (a dimension-free stability theorem would subsume Vestfrid's three papers and be a genuine downstream use of the device, not of the theorem)

open_problems.obstruction_match: Partial. Once a sign function making εf an isometry is found, the 322 theorem finishes (theorem-corollary use). The device itself matters only if the defect argument is run directly on a sign-invariant defect: the opposite-contact step uses −w and is symmetric under w ↦ −w, which is suggestive.
open_problems.adaptation_sketch: Define a phase defect D^±_q(x,y) = min over signs of the 322 defect; attain it in ultrapowers; on directions where the sign is locally constant the return map is defined and the same r = u + M identities hold; use C2's invariant convex set (connected, so a consistent sign exists on it) and C1's contraction to align chords; contradiction as in 322. The real difficulty is global sign coherence (the literature's sticking point), which C1 does not address.

open_problems.title: O3. Mankiewicz-type Tingley problem for boundaries of convex bodies
open_problems.statement: If K ⊂ X, L ⊂ Y are bounded convex bodies and τ : ∂K → ∂L is a surjective isometry (ambient norm metrics), does τ extend to an affine isometry?
open_problems.reference: Posed in the Tingley literature in Mankiewicz's spirit (per search summary of F. Cabello Sánchez, 'A reflection on Tingley's problem and some applications', JMAA 2019; https://dehesa.unex.es/bitstream/10662/19970/4/2019Reflection.pdf could not be fetched). Unverified wording.
open_problems.obstruction_match: The radial-contact machinery (RadialContact.lean) generalizes to Minkowski gauges of any body with an interior point. But the 322 defect D_q compares chords from centres ty and t f(y), i.e. it uses that τ fixes the origin. For non-symmetric bodies there is no distinguished centre, so the hard part (finding the centre map) is outside C1.
open_problems.adaptation_sketch: Reduce to symmetric case when K = -K; otherwise first prove that τ maps some interior 'centre' (e.g. via affine diameters, cf. S4) to a centre of L, then run the 322 argument with gauge radii. Expect failure at the centre step.

open_problems.title: O4. Positive Tingley problem for general ordered Banach spaces / Banach lattices
open_problems.statement: Does every surjective isometry between the positive unit spheres of two Banach lattices (or ordered Banach spaces) extend to a surjective real-linear isometry?
open_problems.reference: Peralta's question as generalized by Leung-Ng-Wong (TAMS 2025; arXiv:2006.08944); Ezumi-Lin-Miura arXiv:2601.17704 (C0(X), 2026); arXiv:2607.10685 (absolutely continuous functions, 2026). URL: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.17704v1
open_problems.status: open in general; known for L^p, C(K), C0(X), von Neumann algebras (abstract-level)
open_problems.obstruction_match: Weak: no antipodes inside the positive sphere, so the opposite contact tb - uw leaves the domain of f. The device does not apply without a replacement for −w (e.g. order-complement directions).
open_problems.adaptation_sketch: Replace the opposite contact by the contact in direction (e - w) for an order unit e when one exists; check whether r = u + M style identities survive. Low expectation.

lean_feasibility.statable_with: Mathlib NormedLatticeAddCommGroup / OrderedAddCommGroup + NormedSpace ℝ, LinearIsometryEquiv

open_problems.title: O5. Tingley's problem for quasi-Banach (p-normed, 0 < p < 1) spaces
open_problems.statement: Does every surjective isometry between unit spheres of two quasi-Banach (p-Banach) spaces extend to a real-linear isometry?
open_problems.reference: Huang-Zhu arXiv:2607.11244 (Schatten classes 0 < p ≠ 2 < ∞, including quasi-Banach); references [26,35] there for ℓ_p-type quasi-Banach cases (not identified).
open_problems.obstruction_match: Same problem shape, but the device's two pillars fail: Hahn-Banach supports (lem:support, used by C2 and the contradiction) can vanish (L_p[0,1]* = 0 for p < 1), and Schauder/Darbo for non-locally-convex spaces is the delicate Schauder-conjecture territory (Cauty 2001). Expected failure; doubles as a negative control.
open_problems.adaptation_sketch: Restrict to p-Banach spaces with separating duals and use p-convex hulls; the contraction estimate (two triangle inequalities) survives with ‖·‖^p, but the convex invariant set does not.

lean_feasibility.score: statable with < 300 lines of new definitions
lean_feasibility.missing: QuasiNormedSpace / p-norm structure and its unit sphere (~150-250 lines)

open_problems.title: O6. Local Tingley: isometries between relatively open subsets of unit spheres
open_problems.statement: If U ⊂ S_X, V ⊂ S_Y are relatively open (connected) and τ : U → V is a surjective isometry, is τ the restriction of a linear isometry X → Y?
open_problems.reference: Cabello Sánchez 2019 (strictly convex spaces: an onto sphere isometry that is the identity on a relatively open subset is the identity; finite-dim strictly convex: linear iff linear on an open set). General local question: status unverified.
open_problems.obstruction_match: Poor: C1 needs the global defect bound over all of S_X and the inverse f^{-1} at the opposite contact, which may lie outside V.
open_problems.adaptation_sketch: Work with small t so that all contacts stay near y; local attainment by ultrapowers of germs. Unclear.

open_problems.title: O7. Figiel-type theorem for into (non-surjective) sphere isometries
open_problems.statement: If f : S_X → S_Y is an isometry (not onto), is there a norm-one linear Q : span‾ f(S_X) → X with Q∘f = id on S_X (the sphere analogue of Figiel's 1968 theorem)?
open_problems.reference: Figiel 1968 (whole spaces); Godefroy-Kalton 2003. The sphere version is recalled from the Cheng-Dong circle of work; not verified this session.
open_problems.obstruction_match: C1 uses f^{-1} at the opposite contact (zPoint := f.symm (radialContact ...)). Without surjectivity this step is undefined; the ℓ∞ counterexample in the negative controls shows a linear extension can fail, but a Figiel-type left inverse is a weaker conclusion.
open_problems.adaptation_sketch: Run the return map in the reverse direction (Y → X) where f^{-1} is only needed on f(S_X) when the opposite contact lands in f(S_X); prove that the extremal set is closed under that operation. Low expectation.

open_problems.title: O8. Affine diameters through interior points of bounded convex bodies in infinite-dimensional Banach spaces
open_problems.statement: Does every interior point of a bounded closed convex body in a Banach space lie on a chord [x,z] with a functional attaining its max at x and its min at z?
open_problems.reference: Finite-dimensional theorem: Hammer 1954 (S4). Infinite-dimensional version: not found as a posed problem (my formulation; status unverified).
open_problems.obstruction_match: Template: aligned chord through an interior centre = fixed direction of a return map; no compactness. Missing: any self-supplied contraction margin (no defect M), which is C1's actual content. In non-reflexive spaces sup-attainment already fails (James), so the statement may be false.
open_problems.adaptation_sketch: Look for an extremal functional (e.g. maximal 'asymmetry defect' of chords through c, attained in an ultrapower) whose positivity supplies a χ-contraction for the direction map. Speculative.

theorem_corollaries: Mazur-Ulam property for every real Banach space (Cheng-Dong question) — immediate restatement.
Tingley 1987: f(-x) = -f(x) for sphere isometries of finite-dimensional spaces.
Kadets-Martín 2012 (finite-dimensional polyhedral spaces) and Banakh 2022 (every 2-dimensional space has the MUP; also arXiv:1911.03767 absolutely smooth planar case).

Class results: Ding (ℓ^p, ℓ∞(Γ)-type), Tan (L^p), Fernández-Polo-Peralta (von Neumann algebras), Mori (preduals), Mori-Ozawa (unital C*-algebras as real spaces), Fakhoury (Schreier spaces, JFA 2025), Maślany (Tsirelson-type T[θ,S_α]), Huang-Zhu (Schatten 0<p<∞, Haagerup L_p) — all become one-line instances (real-linear conclusion).
Object-level rigidity: isometric unit spheres ⇒ linearly isometric spaces, in every dimension (contains Nakamura-Tanaka arXiv:2609.31096, finite-dim, posted 2 days after the 322 manuscript).
For phase-isometry problems (O2), the extension half of every known class result reduces to the 322 theorem once a sign function is fixed.

Lean note: these are measurable as 'instantiate tingley_sphere_isometry_full' (Banakh's 2D theorem is statable now with EuclideanSpace/WithLp in dimension 2), but they measure the theorem's reach, not reuse of the device.

negative_controls.title: N1. Non-surjective sphere isometries into ℓ∞ (proved false)
negative_controls.statement: For separable X with {a_n} dense in S_X, Φ(x) = (1, (‖x - a_n‖ - 1)_n) is an isometry S_X → S_{ℓ∞} (first coordinate 1, others in [-1,1]; sup_n |‖x-a_n‖-‖x'-a_n‖| = ‖x - x'‖). Φ(-x) ≠ -Φ(x), so no linear extension exists.
negative_controls.why_device_fails: zPoint := f.symm (radialContact ...) needs the opposite contact to lie in the range of f; surjectivity is essential to C1 and the counterexample shows it cannot be dropped.
negative_controls.lean: statable now (Mathlib lp (fun _ => ℝ) ∞); counterexample formalizable in ~100-200 lines

negative_controls.title: N2. Uniform (non-isometric) version: Mazur map S_{ℓp} → S_{ℓ2} (proved false analogue)
negative_controls.statement: The Mazur map x ↦ sign(x)|x|^{p/2} is a uniform homeomorphism between the unit spheres of ℓ_p (1 ≤ p < ∞) and ℓ_2 (Mazur 1929; the tool used by Odell-Schlumprecht 1994), yet ℓ_p and ℓ_2 are not linearly isomorphic for p ≠ 2.
negative_controls.why_device_fails: C1 relies on exact distance preservation to force r = u + M and s = p + M (equality in two triangle inequalities); under uniform/bi-Lipschitz control those identities and the contraction margin disappear.
negative_controls.lean: statable now; Mazur map formalization would need lp-space API work (~300 lines)

negative_controls.title: N3. Complex linearity (proved false)
negative_controls.statement: Complex conjugation on S_ℂ (or coordinatewise on S_{ℂ^n}) is a surjective sphere isometry that is not complex-linear.
negative_controls.why_device_fails: The device works with real chords and real scalars t, p, r, s, u; it can only ever yield real-linearity, consistent with the 322 docs ('real linearity rather than complex linearity').

negative_controls.title: N4. Mankiewicz / Mazur-Ulam for balls or whole spaces (device unnecessary)
negative_controls.statement: Isometries between unit balls (or open connected sets) extend affinely (Mankiewicz 1972); onto isometries of normed spaces are affine (Mazur-Ulam, in Mathlib).
negative_controls.why_device_fails: Not a failure but no help: interior points give midpoints directly; a prover with C1 in its library should show zero speedup. Good baseline for the Lean speedup protocol.
negative_controls.lean: Mazur-Ulam is in Mathlib (IsometryEquiv.toRealLinearIsometryEquivOfMapZero); Mankiewicz is statable now

top5.argument: The only target where C1's specific content (the defect M manufactures the contraction margin) is needed and the 322 theorem does not already settle the question. Statable now with UnitSphere + LinearIsometryEquiv. A Lean test: give the prover the 322 library and ask for M ≤ Cε^α for the ultrapower-attained defect; compare with and without ReturnMap*/Alignment. Risks: the exact-isometry lemmas must be re-proved with slack, and the last step (approximate Mazur-Ulam for homogeneous maps) is a separate obstacle that C1 does not touch.

top5.target: S1 Vestfrid's finite-dimensional sphere ε-isometry theorems (ℓ2^n, ℓ∞^n, ℓ1^n)
top5.argument: The measurable known-theorem version of O1: statable now (EuclideanSpace, WithLp ∞/1), finite dimension removes the ultrapower and makes Darbo collapse to Brouwer, so the test isolates the return map + margin. Expected speedup low-med; a positive result would be the first genuine downstream reuse of the device.

Active 2020-2026 literature with class-by-class results and a recently flagged gap (Enami-Matsuzaki 2026). Statable now. Mostly a theorem-corollary use, but the opposite-contact step is sign-symmetric, so a sign-invariant defect run of C1 is a concrete, testable adaptation. Confidence 0.25.

Cheap, statable now, and already isolated in Lean (exists_fixedPoint_of_return_estimate is map-agnostic). Run it to separate the speedup due to the re-proved Darbo/Schauder stack (transfer, N0) from any speedup due to C1. Needed so that O1/S1 results are not misattributed.

top5.target: O3 boundaries of convex bodies (Mankiewicz-type Tingley)
top5.argument: Statable now; the radial-contact layer generalizes to gauges, so the test would show whether C1 transfers once a centre is fixed. Expect failure at the centre-finding step, which makes it informative about the device's scope rather than a likely success.
